text_blocks.snippet: Residents in Central Illinois are currently targeted by fraudulent text messages from fake DMV agencies and phone scams involving impersonated local police.

list.snippet:
Fake DMV and IDOT Texts: Scammers send text messages claiming your license or vehicle registration will be suspended due to unpaid fines, or offering fake fuel rebates, which you can review on the
Illinois Department of Transportation
warning page.

Police and City Impersonation: Callers or fraudulent letters pretend to be local sheriffs, police departments, or city zoning boards demanding money or Bitcoin to clear a fake arrest warrant or invoice.
Package Delivery Phishing: Fraudulent texts using USPS or UPS logos claim a package delivery failed and ask for credit card details.
Practice the pause: Scammers create fake urgency to stop you from verifying facts.

Never click links:
State agencies and police departments never text you to demand payment or threaten arrest.

Report fraud: Forward suspicious text screenshots to the Illinois Secretary of State via ScamAlert@ilsos.gov
.

text_blocks.snippet: If you received a suspicious message or call, tell me what it claimed and how they contacted you so I can help you identify if it is a known scam.
